issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks a CI build workaround into core/setup.py runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: The mmcv pkg_resources problem is a build-time CI issue, but core/setup.py now pins setuptools<82 in install_requires for the hyperopt extra. Every downstream user inherits the cap forever. Keep the workaround in the CI scripts where the FIXME already lives; remove it from the library's runtime contract.

issues.description: Three near-identical setuptools<82 pins with no single source of truth or revert criteria.
issues.detail: env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py each independently assert setuptools<82 referencing mmcv#3325. There is no shared constant and no statement of the condition that flips the cap off. When the upstream fix lands, all three sites must be remembered. Add an explicit revert condition and consolidate.

issues.description: mmdet silently bumped 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 inside a setuptools/mmengine CI fix.
issues.detail: The PR is titled as an mmengine failure fix but also bumps mmdet a minor version and swaps mmengine from a git SHA to PyPI 0.10.7. These are separate risk surfaces bundled under one CI patch, harder to bisect later. Split or justify in the commit message that 3.3.0 is required for compatibility.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation silently couples the build to ambient environment state.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation means mmcv's build now depends on whatever setuptools, wheel, and torch the active env provides instead of the isolated PEP 517 contract. It works because setuptools<82 is pre-pinned and torch is preinstalled by the caller, but the coupling is invisible. Add an inline comment stating the precondition.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the CI fix is directionally correct: pin setuptools<82 to dodge the pkg_resources removal that breaks mmcv's build, and move mmengine off a pinned git SHA. The dominant complaint is scope: the setuptools cap leaked from CI scripts into core/setup.py install_requires, pushing a build workaround onto every downstream user of the hyperopt extra. Secondary concerns are duplication of the pin across three files without a shared revert condition, an unjustified mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump bundled into the same patch, and --no-build-isolation silently coupling mmcv's build to ambient environment state. No architectural rework needed — this is contract hygiene on a CI hotfix.
